clue.text: One reason the performance was canceled — possibly of Crusoe.

definitions.text: One reason the performance was canceled
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: if the cast was away, the show could not go on
second meaning: a shipwrecked person marooned on an island, as Robinson Crusoe was

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into CAST AWAY and it explains a cancelled show; read it whole and it is Defoe's marooned hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A castaway is a survivor of a shipwreck left stranded, and Crusoe is literature's best-known example.

clue.text: Sounds like Santa could be dependent, perhaps.

indicators.note: says the answer is pronounced like the name, though spelt differently

parts.note: Santa Claus, so Claus stands for Santa

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Father Christmas relies on others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' gives a word pronounced like the name Claus. 'dependent' is a grammar term here: a dependent clause cannot stand alone as a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a subordinate clause is called dependent, so it is one kind of this sentence unit.

clue.text: What's the answer? Give up?

parts.note: a riddler's taunt, asking whether you surrender; the answer itself is the word for giving up

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the setter teasing the solver, and the word you are asked for is the very act of surrendering.
explanation.definitionFit: To succumb is to yield or surrender to pressure, which is what giving up means.

clue.text: Weakening one container with the contents of another.

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, meaning one

indicators.note: means the second container goes inside the first, as its contents

parts.note: a bag is a container
a tin is another container

explanation.surface: A recipe step where one vessel's contents are poured into another, diluting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the contents of' gives BATING, one container holding the other, before A. 'another' is a second container, not a pronoun pointing back.
explanation.definitionFit: Abating means lessening in strength or intensity, as a storm does when it dies down.

clue.text: What one doesn't intend to take lying down? Such people might be covered only with extra expense.

definitions.text: Such people might be covered only with extra expense

parts.note: an accident is something that happens without intention
prone means lying flat, face down

explanation.surface: A riddle about someone who will not take things lying down, then a note on insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered' is insurance cover: insurers charge clumsy people a higher premium.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are accident-prone keep having mishaps, so insuring them costs more.

clue.text: Fends off with sticks. (Notes are possibly made on them.)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... off, to fend off, originally by using ..., that is sticks

definitions.text: Notes are possibly made on them
definitions.meaning: second meaning: musical ..., the sets of five lines on which notes are written

explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed second half looks like an aside about jotting notes, but it is the musical sense: notes are written on staves.
explanation.definitionFit: To stave off is to ward off, and a stave is also another word for the musical staff.

clue.text: The oldest urn in Greece shows what the lathe-operator is doing.

indicators.note: means the phrase before it shows, that is displays, the answer within its letters

parts.note: the letters run on across the end of oldest, all of urn and in, and the start of Greece

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek urn shows a craftsman at work on a lathe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' means the phrase displays the answer within it, across 'oldesT URN IN Greece'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe spins wood or metal so it can be shaped, and shaping it this way is called turning.

clue.text: The leading position indisposed to take a possible extract of it.

parts.note: the van, short for vanguard, is the front position
indisposed means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: The front-runner, feeling unwell, takes some medicinal extract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the answer: vanilla extract is a familiar flavouring made from the vanilla pod.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is the orchid pod whose essence is sold as vanilla extract for baking.

clue.text: Underlined what comes up as a matter of course.

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the letters are written from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: desserts come as a course of a meal

explanation.walkthrough: 'as a matter of course' sounds like 'routinely'; it means served as one course of dinner. 'comes up' reads DESSERTS from the bottom of this down entry, backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline a point is to stress it, giving it emphasis.

clue.text: Chief heading the CIA organization, no longer effective.

indicators.note: heading means coming first, so the word for chief goes in front of the rest

parts.note: arch, as in arch-enemy, means chief or principal

indicators.note: organization means the letters of CIA are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A spymaster runs the CIA long after he has stopped being any use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' puts ARCH first. 'organization' looks like part of 'the CIA organization', but it tells you to rearrange C, I and A into AIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something archaic is antiquated, so outdated that it no longer works or applies.

clue.text: Official who finds there's absolutely nothing in the business of creating monopoly.

indicators.note: in means the letter for nothing is placed inside the word for the monopoly

parts.note: to corner a market is to buy up enough of it to control it as a monopoly; a corner is that act
O, the figure zero, is absolutely nothing

explanation.surface: A regulator investigating cartels reports that there is nothing wrong at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside CORNER, a market cornered by one buyer. 'who finds' hints at an inquest, where this official delivers a finding.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner is a public official who holds inquests into deaths whose cause is unclear.

clue.text: What social aspirants are trying to do at clubs might help one reach the heights.

definitions.text: What social aspirants are trying to do at clubs
definitions.meaning: first meaning, split in two: social climbers are climbing, and irons are golf clubs

definitions.text: might help one reach the heights
definitions.meaning: second meaning: spiked frames strapped to boots for scaling poles, trees or ice

explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' looks like gentlemen's clubs for social climbers, but the irons are golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing irons are spiked attachments worn on boots to help a person ascend trees or poles.

clue.text: Tried to learn how to settle the dust when about to perish.

indicators.note: settle means the letters of dust are put into a new arrangement
about means the letters of the word for perish are turned around into a new order

parts.note: to perish is to die

explanation.surface: Someone researched how to damp down dust before dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settle' rearranges DUST into STUD; 'about' rearranges DIE into IED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have studied is to have applied your mind to acquiring knowledge of a subject.

clue.text: Shakespearean wall-hangers.

parts.note: points to the song at the end of Love's Labour's Lost

explanation.walkthrough: Wall-hangers suggests tapestries or portraits; the Shakespeare reference is the winter song in Love's Labour's Lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen spikes of ice dangle from the eaves and walls in winter, as that Shakespearean song describes.

clue.text: How the unwelcome might be thrown out, but you could check the answer.

definitions.text: How the unwelcome might be thrown out
definitions.meaning: first meaning: to throw someone out ... is to eject them completely, with all their belongings
second meaning, read literally: bags and baggage are what a traveller checks in at an airport

explanation.walkthrough: 'check' sounds like checking a solution, but here it means handing in luggage to be carried.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means with all one's belongings, and literally it is luggage that a traveller can check in.

clue.text: One might get off the main track if so treated like a bad boy by some.

definitions.text: One might get off the main track if so
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a train that is ... is moved onto a side track by the points

definitions.text: treated like a bad boy by some
definitions.meaning: second meaning: beaten with a switch, a thin cane once used to punish children

explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is a train, not a person going off the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch is both a railway point that diverts trains and a flexible cane used for punishment.

clue.text: You might find it elapse in Straw Dogs, perhaps.

indicators.note: the answer is something you might find by reshuffling the letters that follow, so they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Time seems to slip by during Peckinpah's film Straw Dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You might find it' says the answer is found by reshuffling 'elapse in Straw'. Straw Dogs reads as the 1971 film title, but 'Straw' joins the fodder and 'Dogs, perhaps' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Water spaniels are breeds of gun dog bred to retrieve game from water, so they are dogs.

clue.text: Puts a point forward, perhaps.

parts.note: reads like proposing an idea in debate, but the point is a blade's tip pushed forward

explanation.walkthrough: 'point' suggests an argument; it is the sharp end of a sword or spear.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrust is to push a pointed weapon forward sharply, as a fencer lunges.

clue.text: The thing a candidate is often found in.

definitions.text: The thing a candidate is often found in

parts.words: The thing a candidate is often found in
parts.note: a candidate still in contention is said to be in this, the contest for office

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'in the running' means still having a chance of winning a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Running is competing for office, so a contender still in with a chance is in the running.

clue.text: A way to hold things, superior to an L-bracket by implication.

parts.note: the letter name em comes one above el in the alphabet
a brace is a bracket, both in carpentry and in printing

explanation.surface: A shelving tip: some bracket beats the plain L-shaped kind.
explanation.walkthrough: An L-bracket is an 'el brace'; the next letter up gives 'em brace'.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace is to hold someone in your arms, a hug being one way of holding.

clue.text: With transportation coming up, sits awkwardly just to remain in being.

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the word is written bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: a bus is a form of transportation

indicators.note: awkwardly means the letters of sits are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: A passenger on an arriving bus sits uncomfortably, just getting by.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'coming up' reads BUS from the bottom as SUB, and 'awkwardly' jumbles 'sits' into SIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To subsist is to continue to exist, often barely managing to survive.

clue.text: Fish-head completely inflexible with cold.

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so take the start of Fish

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken
rigid means entirely stiff, not bending at all

explanation.definitionFit: Frigid means very cold in temperature, as in frigid Arctic air.

clue.text: You'll see it in going west, or on to the city.

indicators.note: says the answer can be seen sitting inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run from the last letter of west through or and on to

explanation.surface: Directions for a traveller heading west, or onward to the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You'll see it in' points inside the words that follow: 'wesT OR ON TO'. 'going' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada and the capital of Ontario.

clue.text: One absorbs a good deal of the spirit of the occasion.

definitions.text: One absorbs a good deal of the spirit of the occasion

parts.words: One absorbs a good deal of the spirit of the occasion
parts.note: spirit is liquor rather than mood: a person who soaks up plenty of it is a drinker

explanation.walkthrough: 'the spirit of the occasion' sounds like festive mood; it is the drink being served.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbiber is someone who drinks, especially alcohol, so they take in much of the spirits.

clue.text: The soil may be turned over, but is not very amenable to treatment.

indicators.note: soil that is turned over is dug and mixed, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A gardener's soil can be dug, yet it stays stubborn whatever is done to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be turned over' is digging here, which mixes the letters of THE SOIL; it is not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hostile is unfriendly and resistant, so they do not take kindly to how they are handled.

clue.text: A very low mark given to what Webster might have been doing.

definitions.text: what Webster might have been doing

parts.note: O, a score of zero, is as low as it gets
a rating is a mark or grade given to something

explanation.surface: A dismal grade is awarded to the work of Webster.
explanation.walkthrough: Webster suggests the dictionary-maker Noah, but it is Daniel Webster, the famous American orator.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Webster was a celebrated US senator renowned for his speeches, so he would be delivering an oration.

clue.text: The prescribed amount for a riotous sea-god.

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters of sea-god are jumbled

explanation.surface: Asking how much medicine to give an unruly Neptune.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosage is the measured quantity of a medicine that a doctor orders to be taken.

clue.text: A dessert that's said to be easily prepared.

indicators.note: preparing something is working it into shape, so the letters of A dessert are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone claims a certain pudding is quick to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A dessert' looks like the thing being described, but 'to be easily prepared' rearranges its eight letters, and 'said' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Asserted means stated firmly or declared, a stronger synonym for said.
